incident_2024_10_08_automation_bug:
ROOT CAUSE: A broken release affecting the Automation Rules feature specifically. On 2024-10-08, Automation Rules usage fell to 409 events against a 7-day baseline daily average of 3,020.1 -- an 86.5% drop -- while every other feature moved +6% to +13% versus baseline (consistent with normal day-to-day variation, not a platform-wide problem). Channel and plan-tier mix show no unusual pattern, which rules out an acquisition or onboarding-side explanation.

CONFIDENCE: High -- the drop is isolated to exactly one feature, on exactly one day, with every other feature in the same window moving in the opposite (slightly positive) direction. That combination is very hard to explain with anything other than a feature-specific outage or a broken deploy.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Check the Automation Rules deploy log for 2024-10-08 for a release that shipped that day; this pattern (single feature, single day, near-total drop) is the signature of a client-side bug or a backend dependency failure specific to that feature, not a demand-side issue -- escalate to the Automation Rules engineering owner directly rather than to growth/marketing.
incident_2025_04_ai_assistant_launch:
ROOT CAUSE: The AI Assistant feature launch. Across 2025-04-14 to 2025-04-16, AI Assistant usage rose to 20,085 events against a 3-day baseline of 11,592 (daily average 6,695 vs. 1,656 -- +304.3%), while every other feature also rose 13-20% over baseline in the same window. The uniform-but-smaller lift across the rest of the product is consistent with general launch-week traffic (new and returning users exploring the app after seeing the announcement), but AI Assistant's +304% is a full order of magnitude larger than any other feature's movement, so it is clearly the primary driver rather than a side effect of the broader traffic bump.

CONFIDENCE: High -- the magnitude gap between AI Assistant (+304%) and every other feature (+13-20%) is too large to be explained by ambient traffic alone, and the timing lines up exactly with the known launch window.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: This is a positive incident, not a risk -- route to Product/Growth as a launch success signal. Recommend tracking whether AI Assistant usage holds above its pre-launch baseline (1,656/day) after the initial spike decays, since a launch spike that fully reverts to baseline within 1-2 weeks would suggest curiosity-driven trial rather than durable adoption, and would change the follow-up marketing plan.
incident_2024_12_paid_social_drift:
ROOT CAUSE: A Paid Social-specific activation-rate decline, not a signup-volume or product-wide problem. Over 2024-12-14 to 2024-12-24, Paid Social's activation rate fell to 42.1% from a baseline of 58.6% (-16.5 percentage points), while every other channel held flat (Organic +1.7pp, Paid Search -0.3pp, Referral +0.0pp). Paid Social signup volume also dipped modestly (2,100 to 1,780 baseline vs. incident), but far less than the activation-rate collapse -- meaning people are still signing up via that channel roughly as often, they are simply not converting to an activated account once they land. That pattern points at something in the post-click experience specific to Paid Social traffic (landing page, onboarding flow variant, or audience-targeting mismatch introduced by a campaign change), not a broader product issue, since every other acquisition channel funnels into the identical onboarding flow and shows no degradation.

CONFIDENCE: Medium-High -- the channel-isolation is clean (only Paid Social moved), but without a campaign-change log this report can identify the symptom precisely and narrow the likely cause category without confirming the exact root trigger.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Check the Paid Social campaign/creative and landing-page change history around 2024-12-01 (the drift's actual onset, a few days before the detector's 5-day-minimum threshold triggered on 12-14) for an audience-targeting or landing-page change; if a change is found, revert or A/B test against the prior version. If no change is found, pull a sample of Dec 2024 Paid Social signups that failed to activate and check for a common onboarding-step drop-off, since that would point to a technical (not marketing) cause instead.
incident_2025_02_webinar_false_positive:
ROOT CAUSE: This is not a product incident. Across 2025-02-11 to 2025-02-13, adoption events rose 91-102% over baseline in every single feature (Automation Rules +91.1%, API Access +101.6%, all others in between), and the channel mix (Organic 38,586 / Paid Search 23,761 / Paid Social 21,055 / Referral 17,070) is almost exactly proportional to each channel's normal overall share of traffic. A uniform, cross-feature, cross-channel lift of this shape is the signature of a broad marketing/awareness event driving more people to use the product generally, not a bug or a channel-specific problem -- this matches Flowdesk's planned Feb 11-13 product webinar week.

CONFIDENCE: High that this should be dismissed as an incident -- a real bug or channel problem produces an isolated, disproportionate movement in one feature or channel; this event moved everything by roughly the same percentage, which a single localized cause essentially cannot produce.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: No engineering or growth intervention needed. Recommend adding known marketing-event dates (webinars, launches, conference weeks) to the point-anomaly detector's exclusion list going forward, the same way the channel-drift detector already excludes known holiday-adjacent windows -- this avoids paging anyone for expected, planned traffic spikes.
